title: Embedset clustering noise resilience survey
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an exploratory evaluation protocol and early findings for how our multilingual embedsets behave under realistic and adversarial input perturbations. The immediate goal is to produce an embedset-level regression test that flags brittle clustering/nearest-neighbor behavior after model onboarding, quantization, or runtime changes.

Scope and motivation:
- Focus: cluster stability and semantic-search relevance under noisy inputs across English, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Russian, and two low-resource languages (Vietnamese, Swahili).
- Why: production customers report that short support queries or noisy OCR transcripts cause search results to degrade unpredictably; we want measurable, repeatable signals rather than ad-hoc manual checks.
- Outcome: a small, reproducible probe suite (<= 5k examples) + thresholding rules for automated regression alerts.

High-level approach:
1) Create base reference embedset: curated canonical documents + canonical queries across domains (support KB, product descriptions, legal snippets, clinical abstracts).
2) Generate controlled perturbations of queries and documents to simulate realistic noise and adversarial cases.
3) Compute metrics on clustering (silhouette, cluster purity, neighbor stability) and search relevance (Recall@k, MRR, semantic-CTR proxy) comparing target model to a gold baseline (current production embed model).
4) Flag regressions using delta thresholds (absolute and relative) and run as part of onboarding pipeline.

Datasets and sampling: (sizes are for the probe suite target)
- Base corpus: 3,200 short docs (200-800 tokens) split across 8 domains: support (800), product (600), legal (400), sales/marketing (300), knowledge-base FAQs (500), biomedical abstracts (200), developer docs (300), small code snippets (100).
- Query set: 1,600 queries (2 per doc on average) designed for varying retrieval difficulty: 60% easy (lexical overlap), 30% paraphrase/semantic, 10% inferential/low-context.
- Language split: EN 50%, ES 15%, ZH 12%, RU 10%, VI 8%, SW 5%. Every query/document pair has a language tag.
- Annotation: ground-truth relevance is binary at doc-level (relevant/non-relevant) with a small multi-relevance subset (topical grades) for MRR calibration.

Perturbation families (generated deterministically with fixed seeds):
A. Noise types mimicking user input:
  - Typo/character-level: random deletion/insertion/transpose (5%/10%/20% severity).
  - Spacing and punctuation removal: collapse punctuation, remove diacritics for languages that use them.
  - OCR artifacts: common confusions (0/1 vs O/I, ligature splits) sampled from real OCR error logs.
  - Case/normalization variants: all-caps, no-case, mixed-case.

B. Linguistic perturbations:
  - Paraphrase injection: back-translation SMT-style (EN->FR->EN) and modern NMT paraphraser with beam diversity parameter.
  - Code-switching: inject single-sentence phrase in another language (esp ES/EN and EN/VI).

C. Adversarial/semantic-level changes:
  - Negation flip: add/remove negation clauses.
  - Add distractor sentence: insert unrelated short sentence from another domain.
  - Semantic compression: truncate context to simulate short chat queries.

D. Quantization/runtime artifacts:
  - Simulated 8-bit and 4-bit quantization encodings using our offline quant pipeline to see embedding drift.
  - Signed-int rounding noise emulation (for hardware-specific kernels).

Metrics and diagnostics:
- Nearest-neighbor stability (NNS): fraction of top-k neighbors retained between baseline and candidate embeddings for same input (k=10,100).
- Rank correlation: Spearman rho on per-query ranking scores for the top-k set.
- Recall@k and MRR: standard retrieval metrics against ground-truth doc list (k=1,5,10).
- Cluster purity: given K clusters from base (K chosen via silhouette elbow), measure purity change and adjusted Rand index (ARI) vs baseline clusters.
- Silhouette coefficient: global and per-language.
- Median cosine shift: distributional change in cosine similarity for relevant pairs.
- Failure-mode counts: counts of 'semantic-hallucination' where an obviously unrelated doc is in top-1 post-perturbation (heuristic + manual review).

Thresholding for regressions (initial proposals, conservative):
- NNS@10 drop > 15% for any language -> warn.
- MRR drop (relative) > 8% for major languages (EN/ES/ZH) -> fail onboarding.
- ARI drop > 0.12 -> fail.
- Silhouette global drop > 0.06 -> warn.

Protocol for a single onboarding run:
1) Compute baseline metrics for canonical inputs (store snapshot).
2) Run candidate model on same inputs, plus all perturbations.
3) Compute metric deltas and produce a regression report (CSV + HTML summary).
4) Surface top 20 queries with largest rank shifts and sample inputs to a reviewer UI for triage.
5) If fail thresholds met, mark model as failing regression gate and attach recommended remedial checks (re-check quantization, re-evaluate prompt handling, check tokenization differences).

Preliminary findings (from exploratory runs on two open models + internal prod model):
- OCR-style character confusions disproportionately impact Chinese and Russian when tokenization boundaries differ — nearest-neighbor stability NNS@10 drops 22% at 10% OCR noise vs 8% in English.
- Paraphrase back-translation preserves Recall@10 reasonably well for EN and ES (~3-6% delta) but fails faster for low-resource languages (VI, SW) where paraphraser introduced unnatural syntax.
- Quantization to 8-bit had small median cosine shift (~0.012) but amplified neighbor instability for short queries (<6 tokens) in the sales/marketing domain (NNS@10 down 12%).
- Code-switching cases produce large silhouette variance within a language cluster — indicates existing embed models do not robustly co-locate mixed-language utterances.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Threshold tuning: should thresholds be per-language or per-domain? Proposal: baseline thresholds per language with domain-aware overrides for biomedical/legal where precision matters.
- Failure triage UI: small prototype needed to let reviewers view "before/after" neighbor lists and raw tokens. Assign to SE team backlog (see JIRA-ENG-6421).
- Sampling refresh cadence: how often to re-sample negative distractors? Monthly vs on each major model change.

Action items (next 6 weeks):
- [Ava] Finalize probe generation code and seed + publish pipeline (GH PR: /embeds-eval/pull/93) — ETA 2 weeks.
- [Ravi] Build lightweight HTML report template and attach top-20 shift table — ETA 3 weeks.
- [Lin] Add tokenization alignment checks and preliminary tokenizer-diff metric to pipeline — ETA 4 weeks.
- [Mariana] Expand low-resource paraphrase set using crowdsource microtasks for VI and SW (budget request in Confluence).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "stability score" composite that combines NNS, MRR, and silhouette into a single scalar for quick gating but keep component metrics available for triage.
- Could augment with synthetic speech-to-text errors using common ASR confusions from customer logs instead of generic OCR.

Appendix: quick reproducibility commands (local dev)
- python tools/generate_probe_set.py --lang en,es,zh,ru,vi,sw --seed 42 --out probes/v1
- python tools/run_embed_eval.py --model candidate.pt --baseline baseline-v3 --probes probes/v1 --output reports/candidate-vs-baseline.csv
- scripts/generate-html-report reports/candidate-vs-baseline.csv --topk 20 --out reports/candidate-vs-baseline.html

References and inspirations:
- Internal: semantic-search-team/errata/ocr-confusions.csv
- External: "Robustness of Embedding Models to Textual Noise" (arXiv 2023)

If you want to iterate on specific perturbation templates or add more domains (e.g., financial filings), leave comments below or tag me. This is intentionally lightweight to get feedback before we formalize into a Confluence runbook.
